- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.3) and prices are trending up, model often underestimates the rise; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by smoothing out immediate peaks.
- If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model often fails to capture the transition; adjust forecast to mean-revert toward recent 7-day average if sentiment shifts >0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period price increases (last 5–7 days of forecast); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model tends to overfit recent noise; use 3–5 day moving average to filter out erratic fluctuations.
